sampling_model.design: A uniform balanced pilot split, balanced complete randomization on \(S_m\), and a pilot-measurable positive-support exact-alpha ellipsoidal mixture on \(T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}=S_m^c\), compared with the full-array oracle on \(T_n^{\mathrm{full}}\).
sampling_model.units: A deterministic triangular array of \(n\) units with complete bounded baselines known before assignment and fixed realized potential outcomes for design-based inference.
sampling_model.treatment: All \(Q=2^{K_f}\) combinations receive equal wave-specific counts.
sampling_model.overlap: The fixed mixture weight \(\eta>0\) gives every balanced assignment positive probability and every unit--combination inclusion positive probability.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional on the parameter-free pilot split and assignment, the likelihood is the product of the observed outcome densities and has random empirical information \(\mathcal I_m(\beta;S_m,Z_{S_m})\). The current arraywise moment assumptions do not imply convergence of this matrix to \(I(\beta)\), so nuisance-efficient estimation and the trace action-regret constant remain conditional targets rather than established properties.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The learned factorial rerandomization procedure achieves the same first-order asymptotic precision as its oracle under suitable conditions.
The pooled binary-arm conditional-minimax-regret plan uses an \(n^{2/3}\) pilot and is approximately worst-case optimal.
The two-stage Bayesian rerandomization procedure learns covariate importance from a pilot and improves first-order precision.
Inverse inclusion weighting gives unbiased estimation under unequal-probability sampling without replacement.
The Horvitz--Thompson estimator is quadratically mean consistent under broad general designs.
Finite-population random partitions obey joint central limit theorems for multiple treatments and vector outcomes.
Fixed symmetric factorial rerandomization yields a truncated-Gaussian joint limit and conservative confidence regions.
Finite-population Gaussian approximation supports large-sample inference for best-choice Mahalanobis rerandomization.
Symmetric rerandomization preserves unbiasedness of ordinary factorial-effect estimators.
Quadratic-form rerandomization criteria admit fixed-geometry precision comparisons and a minimax Euclidean choice.
Sequential superpopulation experiments have first-order semiparametric efficiency bounds under adaptive assignment.

body.tldr: A balanced pilot and a positive-support exact-alpha ellipsoidal mixture yield an exactly unbiased pooled Horvitz--Thompson estimator for the realized factorial vector. The verified asymptotic result is first-order: the full-array and random-complement oracle gains converge after multiplication by wave size to a continuous uniformly positive Gaussian mixture coefficient \(a(\beta)\), giving macroscopic deletion loss \(c a(\beta)/n\) when \(m/n\to c\). Exact accounting decomposes every excess risk into the deletion term \(D_{n,m}\) and learned-action term \(L_{n,m}\), with no third cross-wave term. The pilot likelihood factors exactly through observed outcomes, but the present assumptions do not force its empirical score information to converge to \(I(\beta)\). The square-root pilot constant is therefore established only by a conditional argmin-transfer theorem; its statistical compact-window expansion and remaining endpoint bounds are open finite-boundary and information-limit problems.

project_justification.gap: The closest factorial sample-splitting procedure establishes first-order oracle equivalence but leaves refined learning-sample choice open. Existing binary-arm pilot theory, LAN efficiency theory, and finite-population Gaussian approximation do not supply the score-weighted moving-boundary expansion with exact ties and unequal Horvitz--Thompson inclusions required here.
project_justification.niche: A deterministic complete baseline array and a locally rich bounded outcome chart make it possible to separate three issues cleanly: first-order exact-mixture oracle gain, pilot score-information convergence, and the genuinely second-order finite-boundary comparison.
project_justification.fill: The project proves exact Horvitz--Thompson accounting, a continuous uniformly positive first-order oracle-gain coefficient, an exact pilot likelihood and information audit, the nearly-all-pilot endpoint, and a conditional global argmin transfer. It reduces the proposed second-order frontier to explicit deletion and action-regret comparisons and records the unresolved information and endpoint obligations without claiming their coefficients.

body.related_work: Li and Ding's random-partition central limit theorems support the first-order joint Gaussian limit used for the exact-mixture oracle gain; they do not provide the order-two moving-boundary rate. Han and Deng supply the closest data-adaptive factorial architecture and first-order oracle equivalence, while explicitly leaving refined learning-sample choice beyond their result. Yamin's pooled binary-arm analysis motivates the deletion-versus-action decomposition and conditional argmin architecture, but its \(n^{2/3}\) rate comes from a different regret boundary and is not transplanted here. Armstrong's LAN efficiency bounds apply after an average-information limit is established; the present likelihood audit shows that such convergence is not implied by the current deterministic-array assumptions. Wang and Li's convex-set Gaussian bounds do not control the score-weighted exact-alpha boundary moments at the required order. Horvitz and Thompson justify inverse-inclusion centering, while the exact pooled identity here accommodates randomized ties and unequal inclusions. Menon, Chakrabarti, and Nerella motivate the stable-batch factorial-cycle consumer, but no preregistered square-root pilot rule is claimed until the open statistical premises are proved.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The finite exact-alpha action can change discontinuously when a score coordinate crosses a lattice tie, and exact inclusion probabilities can be unequal. First-order weak convergence absorbs boundary atoms because the limiting Gaussian quadratic form has zero boundary mass, but it supplies no remainder at order \(m/n^2+1/(nm)\). Independently, smooth first two outcome moments do not control conditional score information as a function of the baseline: the rational-grid finite-support witness in the likelihood audit makes the empirical pilot information differ from \(I(\beta)\). These are separate obstructions and neither is assumed away.
body.honest_scope: Established results are exact Horvitz--Thompson unbiasedness and risk accounting, the memberwise one-wave risk bound, common oracle-map convergence, Gaussian boundary regularity, the continuous uniformly positive first-order exact-mixture gain \(a(\beta)\), exact likelihood factorization with an information-limit counterexample, the exact \(D_{n,m}+L_{n,m}\) reduction, the nearly-all-pilot endpoint, and the deterministic conditional argmin transfer. The coefficient \(A(\beta)\), the transfer of \(B(\beta)=\operatorname{tr}\{\Gamma(\beta)I_{\mathrm{eff}}(\beta)^{-1}\}\) to exact finite action regret, the remaining endpoint windows, and the unconditional square-root pilot frontier remain open. The causal estimand continues to be the realized finite-population factorial vector under the stated randomization; the conditional outcome family averages design risk and does not redefine that estimand.
